narrative:
The RaMP enrichment identified **Biological Oxidations** (Reactome R-HSA-211859, FDR 1.8e⁻²⁸) and **Phase I – Functionalization of Compounds** (Reactome R-HSA-211945, FDR 1.5×10⁻⁴) as the top candidate pathways. Membership verification confirmed that benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-epoxide (C14853), coumarin (C05851), methimazole (C07190), and β-mercaptoethanol (C00928) all co-occur in these Reactome annotations with maximum plausibility scores. KEGG reaction-graph traversal found no upstream/downstream relationships between the driver compounds, consistent with them converging on shared *process* pathways (cytochrome P450 oxidation, conjugation) rather than sharing a linear metabolite chain. The data collectively reflect perturbed xenobiotic metabolism.

---

**Affected pathways and key drivers**

The dominant signal is **Biological Oxidations** (R-HSA-211859, fold-enrichment 82.6, 5 matched compounds) and its child term **Phase I – Functionalization of Compounds** (R-HSA-211945, fold-enrichment 82.3, 3 matched compounds). Both are Reactome entries centred on cytochrome-P450–mediated monooxygenation and related redox reactions. A third enriched pathway, **Xenobiotics** (R-HSA-211981, fold-enrichment 207.9), highlights the exogenous-chemical nature of the hits. The **Glutathione conjugation** sub-pathway (R-HSA-156590) was also confirmed for C14853, indicating that benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide — a known carcinogen bioactivation product — is being shunted toward detoxification.

The four principal driver compounds are: **benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide** (C14853), a tier-1 carcinogen adduct requiring glutathione conjugation; **coumarin** (C05851), a CYP2A6 substrate whose hydroxylation is a benchmark Phase I probe; **methimazole** (C07190), a thione drug and flavin-monooxygenase substrate; and **β-mercaptoethanol** (C00928), which participates in thiol-disulfide exchange and Phase II conjugation as a glutathione analog.

**Biological significance**

The convergence of these metabolites on Phase I/II xenobiotic-processing pathways suggests the treatment either induces cytochrome P450 isoforms (CYP1A1/1A2, CYP2A6, CYP3A4) or exposes the system to electrophilic intermediates that demand conjugation. Benzo[a]pyrene diol epoxide is the ultimate DNA-adduct-forming metabolite of benzo[a]pyrene; its elevation in the treatment group implies either increased bioactivation or impaired GST-mediated clearance. Coumarin and methimazole are both metabolised by CYP2A6 and FMO, respectively; their simultaneous elevation suggests a broad induction of oxidative drug-metabolising enzymes. The presence of β-mercaptoethanol points to a compensatory up-regulation of low-molecular-weight thiol buffers. No direct upstream/downstream KEGG reaction relationships were identified among the drivers, which is biologically plausible: these compounds enter Phase I/II from distinct chemical classes but converge on shared catalytic machinery rather than a linear metabolite chain. The finding warrants investigation of CYP450 expression, GST activity, and oxidative stress markers in the experimental model.
